headline: Approved an extension of the Lewiston-Auburn Community Market purchase agreement and an addiction clinic license at 18 Mollison Way.
summary: Speakers during public comment addressed allegations against Councilor Harriman, mobile home park rules, and heating oil costs for seniors. Votes approved a new Department of Community Development and Strategic Initiatives, parking fees for unregistered vehicles, a homeless shelter timeline, and an extension for the Lewiston-Auburn Community Market purchase.
decisions: Approved the election warrant for the November 3, 2026 municipal election and related clerk recommendations, 6-0.
Approved prohibiting overnight parking on a section of Winter Street, 6-0.
Approved reducing parking spaces on a portion of Pine Street for the DeWitt Housing Project, 6-0.
Approved a license for an outpatient addiction treatment clinic at 18 Mollison Way with seven conditions, 5-1.
Approved final passage of the ordinance establishing the Department of Community Development and Strategic Initiatives, 5-1.
Approved final passage of the ordinance on parking unregistered or uninspected vehicles on a public way, 6-0.
Approved first passage of amendments on new special amusement permits and continued the public hearing to the next regular meeting, 6-0.
Approved maximum general assistance amounts for food, housing, utilities, and other expenses, 6-0.
Approved parking fees for unregistered or uninspected vehicles, 6-0.
Approved an amendment to the parking fees policy on use of electric vehicle charging stations in parking garages, 6-0.
Approved extension to the purchase and sale agreement with the Lewiston-Auburn Community Market, 6-0.
Approved timeline and action plan for the Kaydenz Kitchen homeless shelter agreement, 6-0.
Approved appointing Councilor Noble to the Lewiston Youth Advisory Council, 6-0.

1 
 
CITY OF LEWISTON 
 
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 6, 2026 
 
REGULAR MEETING HELD IN THE COUNCIL ROOM AT 7:00 P.M. 
 
THE HONORABLE CARL L. SHELINE, MAYOR, PRESIDING. 
          
PRESENT: Mayor Sheline, Councilors Nagine, Longchamps, Harriman, Noble, Chittim, and 
Martel, City Administrator Bryan Kaenrath, Deputy City Administrator Brian O’Malley, and 
City Clerk Kathleen Montejo. Absent/Excused: Councilor Roy. Note – Per the City Charter, the 
Mayor is able to cast a vote in the absence of a City Councilor.  
 
 
Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. 
 
VOTE (339-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
  
To waive the Council Rules and to allow for unlimited comment time now and to eliminate the 
second Public Comment session at the end of the agenda. Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
 
VOTE (340-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
  
To dispense with the reading of the minutes of the meetings of September 15, 2026, and to 
accept and place them on file as prepared by the City Clerk.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
Susan Longchamps, Ward 2 – Speaking as a member of the public and not as a City Councilor, 
speaking as a mother and a past victim of abuse. Allegations made against a sitting Councilor 
need to be taken seriously. A previous email sent months earlier alerting the Mayor, Council 
President and other city officials of this issue was not acted upon. Has known victim for many 
years, victim has shared her story with her and others. 
 
Eryn Soule, Ward 5 – Asking the City to consider banning the sale of Kratom which is similar to 
prescription painkillers. 
 
Ronnie Paradis, Ward 4 – Worried about cost of heating oil for seniors. Seniors cannot afford 
rising costs. Council should be addressing how to assist seniors. Councilor Harriman should 
resign.  
 
Adam Jones, Ward 2 – Proud of Mrs. Longchamps, takes a lot of strength to make her 
comments.  Encouraged everyone to get out and vote.
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 6, 2026 
                             
2 
 
John Horton, Ward 2 – Against mobile home ordinance. Mobile home parks are mini-cities with 
expenses of road maintenance, utilities, etc.  The ordinance would do financial hard to parks. 
The city has spent thousands of dollars on legal fees regarding this ordinance draft, and a final 
version is still not available. 
 
Zoe Lidstrom, Ward 1 – Supports Councilor Harriman, he is a thoughtful Councilor who always 
responses to citizen communications. These are manufactured allegations. A blogger was 
stalking Harriman’s home.  
 
Lisa Jones, Ward 2 – Harriman has a pattern of denial and refuses to accept responsibility for the 
conduct of his actions.  He is a current State Representative but does not respond to her 
communications, instead, he sends the police to her house. The silence of the Mayor and Council 
shows they condone his actions.  
 
Ben Daley, Ward 1 – Harriman is the victim of unsubstantiated allegations from a blogger. 
Harriman is always supportive of community events. 
 
Jay Zimmerman, Ward 1 – October is National Bullying Prevention Month. Schools are working 
on awareness and encouraging kids to be an Upstander instead of a Bystander. Adults need to be 
role models and teach kids how to respond. 
 
Jimi Cutting, Ward 6 – When was working as a shelter director, heard rumors about similar 
accusations about Harriman. 
 
Matt Agren, Ward 4 – Lewiston is currently a “house divided against itself”. Youth committing 
gun violence with illegal firearms grow up and commit domestic assault. Need schools, law 
enforcement and state justice system to work together to bring control. Parents need to be 
involved. Rounds fired should not be normal. 
 
Ray Toutain, Ward 7 – Besides Wards 2 and 7, this is the worst Council he has seen. Will pay 
for a polygraph test if Councilor Harriman will take one. 
 
Sheri, Ward 7 – Vitriol, ugliness, toxicity, and shaming are turning neighbors against neighbors. 
The Maine Wire blogger is sharing this manufactured story about Councilor Harriman. Harriman 
is dedicated to the community  
 
Mary Hunter, Ward 1 – Knows Harriman as a decent human being. If there is an assumption of 
guilt, follow the appropriate legal process before deciding on guilt. 
 
Katy Crance, Ward 7 – Compliments to Councilor Longchamps for strength to speak her words.  
Harriman is looking away when people speak to him. It is a serious matter when members of the 
public ask an elected official to step down. The people deserve respect. 
 
Ifraax Saciid-Ciise, Ward 2 – Supporter of Harriman, he is responsive, responsible, helpful and a 
great communicator.  Strong supporter of the community. The timing of the allegations is 
questionable, 30 days before the election. Maine Wire made Lewiston look horrible, said 
Lewiston had dirty people.
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 6, 2026 
                             
3 
 
Bob McDonald, Ward 6 – Time for the Council to start to listen to the constituents they 
represent. Bring ICE, DEA, AFT here. Let the Police Chief do her job. There are a lot of non-
profits in town, need some businesses. The Council President should do his job, the Mayor just 
runs the meeting, not gives his opinions. 
 
Martin Chartrand, Ward 3 – Sexual assault is despicable. Hope for healing and justice for the 
victim. These accusations are political, anytime a progressive candidate starts tracking, the 
opponents attack. 
 
Andrew Jones, Ward 2 – The public comment included politicking and the Mayor let it slide and 
did not enforce the Rules. Harriman is responsible to the public. This is another scandal 
involving him the Council has to deal with.  
 
Marcel LeClair, Ward 5 – When someone shows you who they are, believe them. 
 
Mohamad Boulan, Ward 3 – Does not support Harriman. Tired of Maine Wire. Somali 
businesses are closing because of them. They come to Lewiston to scare the people. Don’t want 
to have a divided city. 
 
Councilor Longchamps retired from the meeting at this time. 
 
CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT 
 
The City has announced a new business opportunity grant and there are training sessions on how 
to apply. The Community Engagement and Accountability initiative is now moving to the next 
level of working with state elected officials for changes to state laws. About 40 people attended 
the Red Shop Community Conversation. Public Works is preparing for the winter season. The 
Library will hold a Literary Ball – An Edgar Allen Poe Masquerade. A candlelight vigil will be 
held on Octo 25 for the third anniversary of the mass shooting.  
 
APPROVAL OF ELECTION WARRANT CALLING FOR THE MUNICIPAL 
ELECTION TO BE HELD ON TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 3, 2026 AND 
RECOMMENDATIONS FROM THE CITY CLERK/REGISTRAR OF VOTERS ON 
ACTIONS NECESSARY TO CONDUCT THE MUNICIPAL AND STATE ELECTION, 
NOVEMBER 3, 2026 
 
VOTE (341-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To approve the Order entitled Approvals Necessary to Conduct the November 3, 2026 Municipal 
Election: 
 
Be It Ordered by the City Council that the Election Warrant be issued for the Municipal Election 
to be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, for the purposes of electing the positions of Mayor, City 
Councilor Wards 2, 4 and 6, and School Committee Wards 1, 3, 5, and 7; and
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 6, 2026 
                             
4 
 
To approve the following recommendations from the City Clerk/Registrar of Voters on actions 
necessary to conduct the Municipal and State Election to be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026: 
 
A. That the hours for acceptance of registrations in person only, prior to the November 3rd election, 
as required by MRSA Title 21A, sec. 122, 6A(2), be set at 7:45 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Oct. 14  through 
Nov 2, 2026, with extended hours until 5:30pm on October 20 and until 7pm on October 27. 
 
B. That the names of those persons who register during the closed session for registration shall be 
recorded in accordance with MRSA Title 21A, sec. 122, subsec. 7B, expect the day prior to the 
election when they shall be recorded in accordance with subsec. 7A. 
 
C. Pursuant to Title 21A, sec 759(7), absentee ballots will be processed via central processing at 
City Hall at 2:00pm, 4:00 p.m., 6:00 p.m., and any and all remaining shall be processed at 8:00 
p.m., if necessary, and 
 
D. To authorize the City Clerk to conduct the Mayoral Run-Off election, on Tuesday, December 
15, 2026, if necessary, based upon the results of the November 3, 2026 city election. 
Passed - Vote 6-0 
 
AMENDMENT TO THE TRAFFIC SCHEDULE TO PROHIBIT OVERNIGHT 
PARKING ON A SECTION OF WINTER STREET 
 
VOTE (342-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To approve an Amendment to the Traffic Schedule to prohibit overnight parking on a section of 
Winter Street, as outlined on the attached sheet.  Passed - Vote 6-0 
 
AMENDMENT TO THE TRAFFIC SCHEDULE TO REDUCE PARKING SPACES ON 
A PORTION OF PINE STREET DUE TO THE ROAD CHANGES FROM THE DEWITT 
HOUSING PROJECT 
 
VOTE (343-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To approve an Amendment to the Traffic Schedule to reduce parking spaces on a portion of Pine 
Street due to the road changes from the Dewitt Housing Project, as outlined on the attached sheet. 
Passed - Vote 6-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING ON AN APPLICATION FOR A BUSINESS LICENSE RENEWAL 
FOR MERRIMACK RIVER MEDICAL SERVICES, INC. FOR AN OUTPATIENT 
ADDICTION TREATMENT CLINIC AT 18 MOLLISON WAY 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing.
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 6, 2026 
                             
5 
 
VOTE (344-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
  
To approve the License for an Outpatient Addiction Treatment Clinic for Merrimack River 
Medical Services, Inc. to operate a Clinic at 18 Mollison Way, Lewiston, subject to the following 
conditions: 
  
1. 
 
Provide adequate interior client waiting space to eliminate the need for clients to queue 
or wait for service outside of the building, except for clients waiting for public 
transportation. 
 
2. 
 
Effectively monitor the exterior of the property to ensure that clients do not loiter on or 
adjacent to the property for any purpose other than waiting for the arrival of public 
transportation.    
 
3. 
 
Designate the exit from the clinic that leads to a lobby shared with other tenants within 
the building as an emergency exit only and provide an audible alarm that will sound if 
this exit door is opened. 
 
4. 
 
Applicant will maintain a methadone maintenance program as described in their 
“Treatment Components” and “Program Components”.  The applicant will 
immediately report to the police department any breaches of the security system 
described in the attachment. 
 
5. 
 
Consistent with the applicant’s application, the number of clients shall not exceed 500 
at any given time. 
 
6. 
 
The applicant will annually provide documentation to the City Clerk of the receipt of 
all approvals required by any federal or state agency or department pursuant to federal 
or state law. 
 
7. 
 
The applicant will comply with the requirements of Chapter 22, Article XIV, Section 
22-417 of the Code, requiring the applicant to conduct meetings at the discretion of the 
chief of police and/or his designee.  
 
Passed - Vote 5-1 (Councilor Martel opposed) 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FINAL PASSAGE REGARDING AN AMENDMENT TO THE 
ADMINISTRATIVE CODE TO ESTABLISH THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMUNITY 
DEVELOPMENT AND STRATEGIC INITIATIVES 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing. 
 
VOTE (345-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That the proposed amendments to the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 2 “Administration”, 
Article V “Departments”, Division 1 “Generally” and Division 2 “Department of Community
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 6, 2026 
                             
6 
 
Development and Strategic Initiatives”, receive final passage by a roll call vote. 
Passed - Vote 5-1 (Councilor Martel opposed) 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FINAL PASSAGE FOR AN AMENDMENT TO THE 
TRAFFIC AND VEHICLES ORDINANCE REGARDING UNREGISTERED OR 
UNINSPECTED VEHICLES PARKED ON THE PUBLIC WAY 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing. 
 
VOTE (346-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That the proposed amendment to the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 70 “Traffic and 
Vehicles”, Article IV “Stopping, Standing, and Parking”, Section 70-2 “Definitions” and Section 
70-153 “Parking unregistered or uninspected vehicles on a public way” receive final passage by 
a roll call vote. 
 
Passed - Vote 6-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FIRST PASSAGE REGARDING AN AMENDMENT TO THE 
AMUSEMENTS AND ENTERTAINMENT ORDINANCE REGARDING APPROVALS 
FOR NEW SPECIAL AMUSEMENT PERMITS 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing. 
 
VOTE (347-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That the proposed amendments to the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 10 “Amusements and 
Entertainments”, Article III “Special Amusement Permits”, Division 2 “Permit”, receive first 
passage by a roll call vote and that the public hearing on said ordinance be continued to the next 
regularly scheduled City Council meeting.   Passed - Vote 6-0 
  
PUBLIC HEARING AND APPROVAL OF AMENDMENTS TO THE GENERAL 
ASSISTANCE POLICY FOR ANNUAL AUTHORIZATION OF 
ELIGIBILITY AMOUNTS 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing. 
 
VOTE (348-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That the maximum amounts allowed for general assistance and the maximums allowed for food, 
housing, personal care, utilities, heating fuel, transportation, and recovery residence expenses in
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 6, 2026 
                             
7 
 
the General Assistance Policy, for persons eligible to receive assistance in accordance with the 
standards of eligibility, be adopted as presented, in accordance with HUD guidelines and the 
current Thrifty Food Plan.   Passed - Vote 6-0 
 
AMENDMENTS TO THE MUNICIPAL PARKING FEES POLICY TO ESTABLISH 
FEES FOR UNREGISTERED OR UNINSPECTED VEHICLES 
 
VOTE (349-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve the proposed amendment to the Parking Fees Policy, Policy Manual Number 42, as 
recommended by City Administration and the Police Department. Passed - Vote 6-0 
 
AMENDMENT TO THE PARKING FEES POLICY REGARDING USE OF THE NEW 
ELECTRIC VEHICLE (EV) CHARGING STATIONS IN THE PARKING GARAGES 
 
VOTE (350-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve the amendment to the Parking Fees Policy regarding the use of Electric Vehicle (EV) 
charging stations in the parking garages.  Passed - Vote 6-0 
 
ORDER, AUTHORIZING THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR TO EXECUTE AN 
EXTENSION TO THE PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT WITH THE 
LEWISTON-AUBURN COMMUNITY MARKET, INC. 
 
Seven members of the public spoke in support of this Order and encouraged Council to support 
the plans for the new market. Councilor Chittim noted he is a member of the market but did not 
view it as a conflict of interest. 
 
VOTE (351-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Harriman: 
 
To approve the Order, Authorizing the City Administrator to Execute an Extension to the 
Purchase and Sale Agreement with The Lewiston-Auburn Community Market, Inc.: 
 
Whereas, on January 3, 2024, the City of Lewiston entered into an Option Agreement with The  
Lewiston-Auburn Community Market, Inc. (LACM) to provide the organization with an exclusive  
option to purchase the former Lewiston Police Department Headquarters for the development of a  
community market; and 
 
Whereas, April 1, 2025, the City of Lewiston executed a 6-month extension to said Option  
Agreement; and 
 
Whereas, LACM demonstrated significant progress in raising funding for the $9.9M project; and
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 6, 2026 
                             
8 
 
Whereas, LACM has worked diligently over several years, with City staff, stakeholders,  
community members, the Choice Neighborhood planning and development process, and as a result  
has produced viable and actionable plans for a for-profit, co-operative, property-taxable  
community grocery market, food hub, education center, and community center that will bring  
vibrancy, economic activity, and walkable grocery store access to the city center; and 
 
Whereas, the City Council desires to support economic development projects and growth in the  
tax base vigorously, using all available strategies in a wide variety of economic sectors city-wide;  
and 
 
Whereas, the City has followed the Council-approved disposition process for the properties  
subject to this Purchase and Sale Agreement, which includes certain real estate, together with all  
buildings and improvements, located at 171 Park Street, 294 Lisbon Street, 308 Lisbon Street, and  
324 Lisbon Street, Lewiston, Maine, said premises more fully described in deeds recorded in the  
Androscoggin County Registry of Deeds at Book 1441, Page 22; Book 1894, Page 137; Book  
6374, Page 1; and Book 4148, Page 103, respectively; and 
 
Whereas, LACM and the City’s staff have agreed to terms that include: a sale price equal to the  
$2,000 earnest money deposit previously paid by LACM; a 60-day due diligence period prior to  
closing; and a reversion clause in the deed that provides for the real estate to be returned to the  
City in the event the project is not completed; and 
 
Whereas, the City Administrator executed the Purchase and Sale Agreement with The Lewiston -
Auburn Community Market, Inc., in October of 2025. 
 
Whereas, During the due diligence period, the LACM has completed a Phase 1 Environmental 
Site Assessment (ESA). The assessment identified the potential presence of two underground 
storage tanks and indicated prior land use as a dry cleaner. The Phase 1 ESA recommends 
further investigation through a Phase II ESA, which will be funded by the grant through the 
AVCOG, with the city participating. This process is necessary not only for financing this 
project but also to eliminate any potential environmental risks for the City of Lewiston and 
will take 4-6 months for completion. Findings will be shared with the CC once the 
investigation is complete. 
 
Whereas, the amended provision would: Remove August 31, 2026, financing deadline and 
eliminate the immediate right of the City to require conveyance of the Property without payment. 
Require the Buyer to diligently pursue all necessary financing, including NMTC financing, 
conventional financing, grants, TIF and other public or private sources. Establish a closing 
deadline of seven (7) months from execution of the amended agreement. Require the Buyer to 
commence substantial construction, including demolition where applicable, within six (6) 
months following Closing. Require substantial completion of the community food center within 
eighteen (18) months following commencement of construction. Require City Council approval 
for any material modification or extension of these deadlines. Continuing to require the Property 
to be used substantially as a community food center, consistent with the project presented to the 
City Council. Allow reasonable modifications necessary to satisfy financing, permitting, 
construction, market or governmental requirements, provided the project remains substantially 
consistent with the community food center purpose.
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 6, 2026 
                             
9 
 
Now, therefore, be it ordered by the City Council of the City of Lewiston that: 
Authorize the City Administrator to sign an extension to the Purchase and Sale Agreement with 
The Lewiston-Auburn Community Market, Inc. 
 
Passed - Vote 6-0 
 
ORDER, AUTHORIZING THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR TO SIGN THE TIMELINE 
AND ACTION PLAN WITH KAYDENZ KITCHEN PANTRY, INC. 
 
VOTE (352-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve the Order, Authorizing the City Administrator to sign the timeline and action plan for 
the Homeless Shelter Service Agreement with Kaydenz Kitchen Pantry Inc.: 
 
Whereas, the City desires to have a homeless shelter operated in the City of Lewiston and, 
Whereas, the City Council approved a master services agreement with Kaydenz Kitchen Food 
Pantry Inc. and, 
Whereas, the City has authorized $400,000 per year in funds to Kaydenz Kitchen Food Pantry 
Inc. to operate a homeless shelter for a three-year period for a total of $1.2 million, 
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered By the City Council of the City of Lewiston, that the City 
Council hereby authorizes the City Administrator to sign a timeline and action plan for the 
Homeless Shelter Service Agreement with Kaydenz Kitchen Food Pantry Inc. 
Passed – Vote 6-0 
 
APPOINTMENT OF COUNCIL REPRESENTATIVE TO THE LEWISTON YOUTH 
ADVISORY COUNCIL 
 
Councilor Noble was nominated to serve in this position. 
 
VOTE (353-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To nominate and appoint Councilor Noble to serve as the Council’s representative to the Lewiston 
Youth Advisory Council.   Passed - Vote 6-0 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
The Public Comment session was cancelled earlier in the meeting. 
 
REPORTS AND UPDATES 
 
Councilor Chittim reported he has resigned from the Railroad Board. Councilor Noble asked to 
have a Council workshop on the topic of Kranton. Councilor Nagine noted the Public Health
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 6, 2026 
                             
10 
 
Committee is studying the issue and will report back to the Council on its recommendations.  
 
OTHER BUSINESS 
 
Councilor Chittim asked to have the mobile home ordinance on the next Council agenda. He 
noted the Housing Committee presented three options for the Council to consider. He asked City 
Administration to develop messaging to all residents about the tax lien process. Councilor 
Nagine is concerned about the partisan divisions within the community. He noted it is beyond 
frustrating and the city is in dire straits.  He noted the City of Auburn does not allow current 
City Councilors to run for state office and views it as a conflict. 
  
 
VOTE (354-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To adjourn at 9:30 P.M.  Passed - Vote 6-0 
 
A true record, Attest: 
 
 
 
Kathleen M. Montejo, MMC  
City Clerk 
Lewiston, Maine
